claims.text: RNN models with context outperform RNN models without context on both character and word based inputs for Chinese short text summarization.
Character-based input models outperform word-based input models in short text summarization using RNN architectures.
In Part II of the LCSTS dataset, short text and summary pairs with relevance scores 1 and 2 account for less than 20 percent of the sampled data.
The main training subset (Part I) of the LCSTS dataset contains 2,400,591 Chinese short text and summary pairs.

evidence.description: Table 2 shows RNN with context achieved ROUGE-1 of 0.108 (Char) and 0.087 (Word) compared to 0.061 (Char) and 0.043 (Word) for RNN without context.

Table 2 reports Character-based RNN with context achieved 0.108 ROUGE-1, 0.073 ROUGE-2, and 0.107 ROUGE-L, outperforming Word-based RNN with context which achieved 0.087 ROUGE-1, 0.054 ROUGE-2, and 0.085 ROUGE-L.
The paper notes that the percent of score 1 (942 pairs) and score 2 (1,039 pairs) is less than 20% out of 10,666 total human-labeled pairs.
Table 1 specifies Part I contains 2,400,591 (short text, summary) pairs mined from Sina Weibo.

methodologies.name: LCSTS Dataset Construction Pipeline
methodologies.description: A multi-stage mining process that crawls weibos from verified organization seed accounts on Sina Weibo and applies filtering rules to extract short text and summary pairs.
conditions: Accounts verified with blue V tag and > 1 million followers

methodologies.name: GRU RNN Encoder-Decoder Summarization
methodologies.description: A sequence-to-sequence neural network using GRU units with character or word tokens to generate concise summaries from short input texts.
conditions: Word-based input using Jieba (50,000 vocabulary size)

limitations.text: The scale of existing summarization datasets is usually very small, mostly less than 1,000 documents.
Word-based models produce many UNK tokens in generated summaries due to word segmentation missing out-of-vocabulary entity names.
Modeling the entire short text as a single sequence may be suboptimal given that short texts often contain multiple distinct sentences.

future_work.text: Exploring hierarchical RNN architectures to handle short texts containing multiple sentences.
Addressing the rare word problem for word-based neural generative summarization models.
Constructing a large-scale document summarization dataset from naturally annotated web resources.
